page: Microsoft Azure E104i_v5 is an isolated, memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system runs an Intel Xeon 8370C processor based on the x86_64 architecture, providing 52 physical cores and 104 dedicated vCPUs with hyperthreading at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz. Memory resources total 672.0 GB of RAM, delivering 6.46 GB per vCPU. Hardware cache provisions include 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. Supported instruction sets include AVX, AVX-512 (F and VNNI), and cryptographic accelerations including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance contains zero GPUs and does not bundle local disk storage.

Benchmark results demonstrate upper-tier multi-threaded and memory throughput. The server achieved 100,833.46 in stress-ng multi-core testing and a PassMark CPU score of 79,491.91, placing both in the top 25%. Uncached large-block read memory bandwidth reached 334.7 GB/s, while cached read bandwidth scored 5,458.86 GB/s. In-memory execution is confirmed by a Redis SET rate of 93.05 million operations per second and high multi-threaded bzip3 decompression throughput of 470.08 GB/s. Extended instruction tests and hardware encryption evaluations reached top percentiles, with PassMark encryption scoring 93,156.86 in the top 10%.

Single-core performance is moderate relative to the dense multi-core capacity. Single-threaded metrics, including a Geekbench single-core score of 1,708.0 and stress-ng single-core score of 1,899.78, place within the middle 50% tier. Similarly, LLM inference text generation speeds scale down as model size grows, falling to 2.67 tokens/sec on 70B models due to the absence of dedicated accelerators. Because local storage is absent, all persistent input/output requires remote block or network-attached volumes.

The E104i_v5 yields balanced cost efficiency for enterprise footprints requiring high memory density, substantial memory bandwidth, and strict isolation without the cost overhead of dedicated GPU silicon. It is suited for large relational databases, distributed in-memory data grids, Redis deployments, enterprise resource planning systems, and large-scale data processing workloads.
